newsitem.title: INDIA: Coalition governments here to stay, India PM says.
newsitem.headline: Coalition governments here to stay, India PM says.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who has led a fragile 13-party alliance for seven months, said on Sunday that the country would continue to have coalition governments in the near future.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Deve Gowda as telling a public rally in his southern home state of Karnataka that if Italy could have 74 governments in 76 years, there was no reason to worry if Indian governments do not complete their terms.
Some of Deve Gowda's United Front allies say his government, sworn in on June 1 last year following inconclusive elections, would not survive its five-year term.
"Coalition politics will continue in India," Deve Gowda told the rally, adding that the period of single-party rule in India was over.
The United Front coalition government is shored up by the Congress party which has ruled India for all but five years since independence from Britain in 1947.
All of India's non-Congress governments have been formed with either a coalition or merger of disparate groups.
Deve Gowda's government has communist ministers for the first time in 50 years.
